analysis.note: Ablative singular of the compound. Internally yathābhimata contains abhimata, a past participial form of abhi-√man, “desired/approved”; Vyāsa construes it as the object to be meditated on, not merely as an adverbial manner.

verification.detail: compound stem yathābhimatadhyāna as Napumsaka/Panchami/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

options_considered: “in whatever manner one wishes,” taking yathābhimata adverbially
“desired meditation,” taking abhimata as qualifying dhyāna itself
“meditation on whatever object is agreeable/chosen,” taking abhimata as the object of dhyāna
justifications.chosen: yathābhimata denotes “whatever is agreeable/chosen” as the meditation-object.

evidence.translation: Whatever is just agreeable/chosen, just that one should meditate on.

justifications.chosen: The compound is understood as a tatpuruṣa headed by dhyāna: meditation whose object is the yathābhimata vastu.

evidence.translation: Whatever is just agreeable/chosen, just that one should meditate on.

justifications.decision: Force of the ablative and the supplied effect
options_considered: bare nominal phrase without supplying the sūtra-contextual result
justifications.chosen: The ablative -dhyānāt has instrumental/causal force, “through/from meditation,” with the implied result of steadiness supplied from the bhāṣya.

evidence.quote: tatra labdhasthitikam anyatrāpi sthitipadaṃ labhata iti.
evidence.translation: There, having acquired stability, [it] obtains a footing of stability elsewhere as well; the printed labhata is likely an unproofread form for labhate.

justifications.chosen: vā is the indeclinable alternative particle, “or.”

translation: Or, through meditation (dhyāna) on just whatever is agreeable/chosen (abhimata) to one, [the mind becomes steadied].
one_shot_delta: Without Vyāsa’s gloss, one might translate yathābhimatadhyānāt as “by meditating however one likes,” making yathābhimata describe the manner of meditation; the commentary instead makes the agreeable/chosen thing the object: yad evābhimataṃ tad eva dhyāyet.
A commentary-blind rendering might miss the practical point of the aphorism: the chosen-object meditation is a way to gain stability there and then obtain steadiness elsewhere too, as line 2 states.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 segments yathā / abhimata / dhyānāt as separate analytical items. I treat the printed pada yathābhimatadhyānād as one inflected compound, pausal yathābhimatadhyānāt, because -āt + vā gives the printed sandhi -ād vā and because Vyāsa glosses the whole by a single predication, yad evābhimataṃ tad eva dhyāyet.
commentary_lines: tatra labdhasthitikam anyatrāpi sthitipadaṃ labhata iti.
